findings.title: Ad hoc filters and variables are applied again on every split sub-request
findings.body: The new `applyTemplateVariables` mapping in `runSplitQuery` runs before the sub-requests are built, but each sub-request is still sent through `datasource.runQuery` (querySplitting.ts:180), which calls `super.query` (datasource.ts:350-352). `DataSourceWithBackend.query` then calls `this.applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` again for each target (DataSourceWithBackend.ts:151, 185). The sub-request keeps `filters` because it is a spread of the request (querySplitting.ts:174). So the ad hoc filters are applied twice on the plain split path. Before this PR they were applied once, in the backend step. On the shard path the same targets go through `runSplitQuery` again (shardQuerySplitting.ts:163), so the filters are applied three times (shardQuerySplitting.ts:52, querySplitting.ts:299, DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185). `addLabelToQuery` does not dedupe for pipeline label filters: `addFilterAsLabelFilter` appends a new `| key=`value`` stage each time (modifyQuery.ts:527-537). Stream-selector matchers are deduped by `labelExists` (modifyQuery.ts:494-497), so the duplication is limited to ad hoc filters on non-selector labels in queries that have a parser. The filter is idempotent, so returned rows should not change, but the query sent to Loki and shown in the query inspector differs from the non-split path. The second pass also re-runs `templateSrv.replace` over text that was already interpolated, so a variable value containing `$name` can be expanded again. Fix: apply templating at one point only, and make sure the sub-request handed to `runQuery` is not templated again.
findings.originReason: In the base, `runSplitQuery` did not template its targets, and the shard path called `interpolateVariablesInQueries` without filters. The extra filter applications were added by this diff.

verification.reason: `runSplitQuery` now calls `applyTemplateVariables` on its targets. Each sub-request is a spread of the request, so it keeps `filters`, and it goes to `datasource.runQuery` → `super.query`. There `DataSourceWithBackend.query` calls `this.applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` again. `addFilterAsLabelFilter` appends a new `| key=`v`` stage on each pass without deduping. On the shard path a third pass comes from `runShardSplitQuery`. In the base, the split path applied ad hoc filters once, in the backend step, and the shard path's frontend interpolation got no filters.

findings.title: Test pins the redundant template calls and no test checks that filters are applied once
findings.body: `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` counts one call in `runShardSplitQuery` plus one per each of the four sub-requests inside `runSplitQuery` (querySplitting.ts:299). That count encodes the repeated application described in querySplitting.ts:299 and will need to change once it is fixed. The new tests do not catch the problem either: `runQuery` is mocked in both new tests (querySplitting.test.ts:83, shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:92), so the templating inside `DataSourceWithBackend.query` never runs, and no test passes `filters`. Suggest a test that passes one ad hoc filter, leaves `runQuery` unmocked or inspects its input, and asserts the filter appears exactly once.

verification.reason: The count of 5 is one call in `runShardSplitQuery` plus one per `runSplitQuery` invocation (4 sub-requests with one target each), so it pins the repeated templating. Both new tests mock `runQuery` and pass no `filters`, so neither would catch the duplicated ad hoc filter.

findings.title: Shard path now defers $__auto to the backend for each time-split chunk
findings.body: Before this PR, the shard path resolved `$__auto`, `$__range` and `$__interval` on the frontend with `request.scopedVars` through `interpolateVariablesInQueries` (datasource.ts:436-443). `applyTemplateVariables` removes `__auto`, `__range` and `__interval*` from the variables (datasource.ts:1113-1125), so these are left for the backend. `runSplitQuery` then splits each shard sub-request by day (querySplitting.ts:316). The comment at querySplitting.ts:285-287 says deferring `$__range` to the backend inside a split sub-request gives the wrong value, which is why `$__range` queries are kept out of time splitting. `$__auto` has no such guard. Is it intended that `$__auto` in shard-split queries now takes its value from each sub-request's range rather than the full request range? I did not read the backend (`pkg/tsdb/loki/step.go`, referenced at querySplitting.ts:360), so I cannot confirm the resulting value.

verification.reason: In the head, `$__auto` is left to the backend, which replaces it with the step it computes for each sub-request. But I could not find frontend code that puts `__auto` into `request.scopedVars`, so it is unclear whether the base shard path ever resolved `$__auto` on the frontend. If it did not, nothing changed for `$__auto`, and the head simply matches the base's plain split path.

contracts.action: runSplitQuery now applies applyTemplateVariables to every target before partitioning (ad hoc filters, step and legendFormat resolved)
contracts.equivalent_path: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/datasource.ts:350-352 (runQuery -> super.query) and packages/grafana-runtime/src/utils/DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185, the existing single templating point for every query
contracts.before_after: Before: raw targets reached runSplitGroupedQueries and were templated once, inside DataSourceWithBackend.query for each sub-request. After: targets are templated in runSplitQuery, and then again in each runQuery call. The resolved expr and step are used for the log/metric partition (querySplitting.ts:301) and for the step-based chunking (querySplitting.ts:327-329, 336-339).
contracts.visible_effect: Ad hoc label filters on non-selector labels in queries with a parser are repeated in the query text sent to Loki. A step of `$step` now resolves to its value before calculateStep, instead of falling back to the interval-based step.
contracts.failure_mode: applyTemplateVariables now runs synchronously inside datasource.query() before the Observable is created (datasource.ts:336-339). Before, the same templating ran inside the Observable's subscription (querySplitting.ts:180, 211-212), so an error there reached the subscriber. Now a throw from addAdHocFilters (modifyQuery.ts:154-156 throws on an empty key) escapes query() directly.

contracts.action: runShardSplitQuery templates targets with applyTemplateVariables instead of interpolateVariablesInQueries
contracts.equivalent_path: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/datasource.ts:429-447 (interpolateVariablesInQueries, the previous call) and public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/datasource.ts:1110-1141 (applyTemplateVariables, which DataSourceWithBackend uses)
contracts.before_after: Before: expr was interpolated with request.scopedVars (including __auto, __range, __interval), datasource was forced to this.getRef(), no ad hoc filters were added, and step and legendFormat were left raw. After: __auto, __range, __interval and __interval_ms are removed from the variables and passed through for the backend (datasource.ts:1113-1125); ad hoc filters are added to expr (1127-1130); step and legendFormat are interpolated (1132-1133); the datasource ref is no longer rewritten. The stream-shard values are fetched with a selector that now includes the ad hoc filters (shardQuerySplitting.ts:252-258).
contracts.visible_effect: Shard values are selected with the ad hoc filters included. $__auto, $__range and $__interval in shard-split queries are resolved by the backend for each sub-request rather than by the frontend against the full request range (see finding on shardQuerySplitting.ts:52).
contracts.failure_mode: fetchLabelValues errors are still caught and the query falls back to an unsharded group (shardQuerySplitting.ts:270-275). The synchronous templating path is the same as in the runSplitQuery entry.
contracts.open_question: Does the backend's resolution of $__auto, $__range and $__interval for a time-split sub-request (querySplitting.ts:316, 338) give the same value that the frontend resolution gave before this PR, for shard-split queries?

contracts.action: applyTemplateVariables runs for every target in the split paths, with no check for a target that names another datasource
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/grafana-runtime/src/utils/DataSourceWithBackend.ts:161-176, where a target with another datasource sets shouldApplyTemplateVariables to false and passes through untouched
contracts.before_after: Before: the split path did no templating, so DataSourceWithBackend's guard decided whether a target was templated. After: runSplitQuery templates every target with Loki's templateSrv and addAdHocFilters, without that guard. The shard path already did this before this PR (interpolateVariablesInQueries had no guard), so this is new only for the plain split path.
contracts.visible_effect: A target that names another datasource, if it reached Loki's query(), would get Loki's variable replacement and label injection in its expr.
contracts.failure_mode: Unknown. I did not establish that Loki's query() can receive a target with another datasource.
contracts.open_question: Can LokiDatasource.query() receive a target whose datasource is a different instance, for example in a mixed panel? If it can, the new split-path templating needs the same guard.

summary: Part 1 of 1 (four Loki split-query files). The main defect is that the new `applyTemplateVariables` calls in `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery` duplicate the templating that `DataSourceWithBackend.query` already does for each sub-request. Ad hoc filters are therefore applied two times on the plain split path and three times on the shard path. The duplication shows in the query text only for pipeline label filters, because stream-selector matchers are deduped. Results are not expected to change since the filter is idempotent. The new tests mock `runQuery`, so they cannot catch this, and one test pins the redundant call count. Two open questions remain: whether the shard path's new deferral of `$__auto` to the backend changes values per time chunk, and whether the split path needs the foreign-datasource guard that `DataSourceWithBackend` applies. I did not build or run anything; I checked the code by reading it.
